newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: 13 burned to death in Malaysia bus-truck collision.
newsitem.headline: 13 burned to death in Malaysia bus-truck collision.

text.p: Thirteen Singaporeans burned to death and 12 were injured on Tuesday when their tour bus rammed into a truck parked on the side of a highway near the Malaysian capital.
A police spokesman told reporters all the passengers were Singapore nationals on their way to Genting Highlands, a hilltop casino resort that is popular with residents in neighbouring Singapore.
A seven-year-old boy, a 10-year-old boy and a 10-year-old girl were among those killed, police said.
Both vehicles caught fire immediately after the bus slammed into the truck, which was carrying scrap metal, the spokesman said.
Sam Wei Jie, 10, who was among those injured, said his father carried him out of the flaming bus after the early morning incident.
"My father carried me out and put me on the side of the road but I can't remember what happened after that. There were flames all over the bus," he said.
The boy's mother, aunt and grandfather are believed to be among the dead, hospital officials said.

His grandmother, Lee Ah Neo, was taken to hospital with slight injuries. It was not immediately clear if the boy's father, who may have tried to rescue other members of the family, was among the survivors, hospital officials said.
The bus driver, identified as Rosni Faat, has been detained for investigation, the police spokesman said.
The truck driver, who survived without injuries, gave police a statement and was released.
The accident occurred at 4.30 a.m. local time (2030 GMT) outside the town of Nilai on the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban highway.
